questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
print(sorted({x % 4 for x in range(10)}), {1, 2}.issubset({1, 2, 3}), {1, 2}.isdisjoint({2, 3}))
questions.exp: Remainders mod 4 are 0-3; {1,2} is a subset of {1,2,3}; it shares 2 with {2,3}, so not disjoint.
Two pushes and one pop leave one element on the stack.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
def mk(n):
    return [lambda x, i=i: x + i for i in range(n)]
fs = mk(3)
print([f(10) for f in fs])
questions.exp: The default argument i=i captures each loop value, so the lambdas add 0, 1 and 2.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a keyword in Python 3?
questions.exp: Python uses if/elif/else without a 'then' keyword.

questions.q:
Statement I: The finally block of a try statement executes whether or not an exception occurs.
Statement II: The else block of a try statement executes only when an exception is raised in the try block.
Which is correct?
options: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
questions.exp: finally always runs; else runs only when the try block completes without an exception.

questions.q: Which statement best describes dynamic typing in Python?
options: Variables must be declared with a type before use
The type of a variable is determined at run time by the value it refers to
A variable can never be reassigned to a different type
Types are checked only at compile time
questions.exp: Names are bound to objects; the type belongs to the object and a name may be rebound to any type.

questions.q: What happens when an existing text file is opened with open('notes.txt', 'w')?
options: The new text is added at the end
questions.exp: Mode 'w' truncates an existing file; 'a' appends and 'x' raises FileExistsError.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
print(type(3/2), type(3//2))
questions.exp: The / operator always gives a float, while // on two ints gives an int.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({'n': ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'], 's': [50, 70, 60, 90]})
print(df.sort_values('s', ascending=False).head(2)['n'].tolist(), df['s'].max() - df['s'].min())
questions.exp: Top two scores are 90 (D) and 70 (B); the range is 90-50=40.
i takes 3, 7, 11, 15, 19 which is five values.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
print(10 > 5 > 2, 10 > 5 > 7, not 1 and 0, 1 or 0 and 0, "a" in "cat" and 3 not in [1, 2])
questions.exp: Chained comparison; (not 1) is False so 'and' gives False; 1 or (0 and 0) is 1.
